items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — customer had to ask her first, and she only answered

Agenda statement had no confirmation request — the 'okay?' landed on the accuracy sentence, then she immediately moved on with 'Alright, so let me just go through the information' without waiting for a yes
Never asked about packing needs at all
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
Never stated the hourly rate per mover per hour
Never covered what's included — gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools
Never mentioned disassembly/reassembly is included, and never asked whether anything needed to come apart in the bedroom
No No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) mention
No 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees)
Clock section almost entirely skipped — no 'clock starts on-site when the contract opens', no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no 'prep before move day shortens the move and lowers the bill', no consolidation examples, no take-a-carload tip. Customer volunteered that he'd have boxes stacked three high for a dolly, which was a wide-open door for it
No confirmation email explained for this call — the only email mentioned was the Meet Your Mover email
No 'bolded list at the top of the email' and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
No hours of operation or specific way to reach the team — only 'we're always here for you'
No school-bus/equivalents reference to make the time estimate concrete
Used the customer's name ('James') only once, at the open — defaulted to 'sir' for the rest of the call
top_strength: Genuinely good estimate work: she caught that a 100-foot walk at the origin would eat time, proactively extended the reservation from 3.5 to 4 hours, and immediately defused the cost fear by explaining the move is time-based so he only pays for what's used. That is exactly the estimate-accuracy behavior the scorecard is trying to produce.
coaching_note: Add the Save Your Ass prep speech to the kickoff-call script — it is worth 10 points and it directly shortens the move, and this customer was already prepping boxes and would have run with it. Second, treat the kickoff call as the last chance to land the differentiators (No Worries coverage, On-Time Guarantee, no hidden fees) rather than assuming the website covered them.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, reassuring and consistently polite — 'no worries', 'you don't have to worry', 'we're super excited and grateful' — and the customer ended the call upbeat and volunteering to help the crew with the gate, though the flow was a bit scripted and leaned on 'sir' instead of his name.
